elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes.

elements.quote: Of 18,783 articles retrieved, 64 fit the inclusion criteria. Qualitative designs were most commonly used for evaluation (48%), with individual interviews as the predominant data collection method.
elements.reason: Reports number of studies and some characteristics, but no participants mentioned.

elements.quote: Of the 64 studies, 44% used a framework, 26% used a model, 11% used a tool, 5% used an instrument, and 14% used theory as their primary approach to evaluate sustainability. Most studies (77%) did not measure sustainability outcomes, rather these studies focused on sustainability determinants.
elements.reason: Presents some results but not detailed for each main outcome with studies and participants.

No group comparisons are made in the abstract or evidence.

elements.quote: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used. There is a disconnect between evaluating the factors that may shape sustainability and the outcomes approaches employed to measure sustainability.
elements.reason: Summarizes limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: Provides general interpretation and implications of the results.
Primary source of funding is not specified in the abstract.
Register name and registration number are not provided in the abstract.

elements.quote: Background: There is limited evidence to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for healthcare improvement. It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used.
elements.reason: The abstract describes the current limited state of knowledge and specific uncertainties about sustainability evaluation approaches.

elements.quote: Through an integrative review, we aimed to identify approaches to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) and sustainability outcomes. Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract explains the aim and importance of the review for advancing the field.
Similar reviews are cited in the discussion section, but the introduction sections provided do not explain the need for the current review in context of existing syntheses.
The review focuses on evaluating sustainability approaches, not on intervention effects.
The review is methodological and does not assess a specific complex intervention or delivery context.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare.
elements.reason: Objectives are explicitly stated, but no relevant question-formulation framework is reported.
The review is not focused on intervention effects; it is about evaluation approaches, so planned comparisons using PICO are not applicable.

elements.quote: In the first screening stage, one reviewer (RF) independently screened the abstracts and titles of all the citations retrieved from the database searches. A second reviewer (AB) independently screened a randomly selected 10% of all titles and abstracts to verify selection for inclusion or exclusion. In the second stage, two reviewers (RF and AB) independently screened all full-text articles that had passed first-stage screening.
